findings.title: Log assertion still racy: unrelated 'lightning*' icon names would match
findings.description: The scoped refutation uses an unterminated string fragment ~s(unknown icon name "lightning) with no closing quote. Any concurrently running test that logs an unknown icon whose name merely starts with "lightning" (e.g. "lightning-slash", "lightning-a") would still trip this refute, reintroducing the same cross-test flakiness the comment says it is fixing. Since the test asserts the row renders the plain "lightning" icon, the refute should match the full quoted name.

findings.title: Root cause of shared-log flakiness not addressed (global log capture)
findings.description: The comment correctly identifies that with_log/1 (ExUnit.CaptureLog) captures the global Logger and that concurrent tests at max_cases: 32 can bleed log output into each other's captures. Narrowing the string match reduces the collision surface but does not eliminate it: another test exercising the same "lightning" icon (or this test's helpers) could still log the message and cause a false failure, and conversely this test could pass even though its refute matched nothing due to a message-format change (e.g., if the log wording changes, refute log =~ ... silently always passes). Consider making these log-asserting tests async: false, or asserting positively on expected log content and verifying the absence of the warning via a more robust mechanism (e.g., a dedicated Logger handler/metadata filter keyed by test pid).
findings.suggestedFix: Mark log-capturing tests as async: false, or filter captured logs by test-specific Logger metadata (e.g., $callers / test pid) before asserting.

findings.title: Partial icon-name match can still collide with similarly-prefixed icons
findings.description: The new assertion uses a prefix match: `log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning)`. This scopes the check better than before, but a concurrent test rendering an icon such as `lightning-fill` or `lightning-bolt` would still produce a log line containing `unknown icon name "lightning...` and trip this refute, reproducing the same flakiness the comment describes. The same applies if the log format ever drops the opening quote or reorders fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Match the full exact message including the closing quote, e.g. `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")`, or use a regex anchored to the exact icon name, e.g. `refute log =~ ~r/unknown icon name "lightning"/`. Even more robustly, capture the log with Logger.capture_log around just this render instead of the global with_log.

findings.title: Log assertion still race-prone under async: true; capture_log scoping preferred
findings.description: The change narrows the refute to the icon name rendered by this test to avoid flakes from concurrent tests emitting `unknown icon name` for other icons. However, if any concurrent test also renders a `lightning`-family icon (e.g., `lightning-fill` — note the pattern `~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` matches any name starting with "lightning"), the same cross-test contamination flake returns. A more robust fix is to disable async for this test module, or use `ExUnit.CaptureLog.capture_log/2` around only the render call, or tag the test with `@tag capture_log: true` and assert on process-scoped captured output where possible.
findings.suggestedFix: Either match the exact rendered name including the closing quote, e.g. `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")` (and also check "lightning-fill" explicitly if relevant), or restructure the test to capture logs only around the specific render so the assertion is not affected by concurrent tests.

findings.title: Prefix match without closing quote weakens the assertion's precision
findings.description: `~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` intentionally omits the closing quote, so it matches both `"lightning"` and `"lightning-fill"` (and any other future `lightning-*` variant). If the intent is to only fail when *this row's* icon is unknown, the broad prefix could still produce false failures if a sibling test renders `lightning-fill` unvendored, or false confidence if the exact name under test changes. Being explicit about which names are expected to be vendored makes the test intent clearer.
findings.suggestedFix: Use exact-name refutes: `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")` and, if the fill variant is also expected to be vendored by this test, add `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning-fill")`.

findings.title: Icon name match is an unclosed prefix, not an exact name
findings.description: The scoped refute uses `~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` without a closing quote, so it is a prefix match. Any concurrent (or same-test) log for a longer name such as `"lightning-fill"` or `"lightning-slash"` would still satisfy `=~` and fail this test, partially undoing the isolation goal described in the comment. Prefer matching the full quoted name.

findings.title: Global log capture remains brittle; prefer per-test capture_log
findings.description: The fix correctly narrows the assertion to the icon this test renders, which mitigates cross-test interference. However, `with_log/1` still captures the global Logger, so a concurrent test that also fails to render a `lightning` icon (e.g., a regression in the shared icon component) would still trip this test's refute — a false attribution. Additionally, the assertion depends on the exact log message format `unknown icon name "..."`, which will silently stop matching if the logging call site changes its wording or quoting style. Consider tagging the test with `@tag capture_log: true` (ExUnit's built-in per-test log capture) if compatible with the LiveView process, or asserting on structured log metadata rather than message text.
findings.suggestedFix: If feasible, use ExUnit's `capture_log` test tag for per-test isolation; otherwise keep the scoped match but note the residual coupling to the log message format.

findings.title: Regex/substring assertion is fragile and may still match unintended log lines
findings.description: The new assertion `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` uses a plain substring match (via `=~` with a string on the right-hand side). This will match any log line containing the substring `unknown icon name "lightning`, including hypothetical variants like `"lightning-fill"` or `"lightning-other"`. While this is an improvement over the previous bare `"unknown icon name"` check, it could still produce false negatives if another concurrent test renders an icon whose name *starts with* `lightning`. Consider using a more precise pattern (e.g., a regex anchored to the exact icon name rendered by this row) or asserting on the specific log entry structure.
findings.suggestedFix:
Use a regex that anchors to the full icon name, e.g.:
```elixir
refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")
```
or if the exact icon name is known:
```elixir
refute log =~ ~r/unknown icon name "lightning"/
```
This ensures the closing quote is part of the match, preventing prefix collisions with names like `lightning-fill`.

findings.title: Comment explains a flaky-test workaround rather than fixing the root cause
findings.description: The comment documents that `with_log/1` captures global Logger output and that concurrent tests can interfere. While scoping the assertion is a reasonable mitigation, the underlying issue — a shared global logger capture in a highly parallel test suite — is an architectural concern. If this pattern of flaky log assertions recurs, consider isolating log capture per test process (e.g., via a custom Logger backend or `:logger` handler added/removed around each test) rather than progressively narrowing substring matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Track a follow-up to provide per-test log capture isolation (e.g., a test helper that attaches a temporary `:logger` handler scoped to the calling process) so assertions can remain broad and deterministic.

findings.title: Log-capture assertion remains inherently racy under concurrent tests
findings.description: The change narrows the refute to a specific icon name to reduce flakiness from cross-test log bleed, which is a reasonable mitigation. However, the underlying race remains: another concurrent test could also render an icon whose name starts with "lightning" (e.g., "lightning-a", or a legitimately unvendored "lightning-slash"), producing a false failure; conversely, this test's own defect could be masked if capture is scoped incorrectly. A more robust approach is to run this test with `async: false`, or to assert on the rendered output/telemetry rather than global Logger content.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider marking the test module `async: false` for log-capture assertions, or use `ExUnit.CaptureLog.capture_log/2` with a function scoped to this render and assert on the returned string only. Alternatively, match the full quoted icon name: `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")` and `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning-fill")` to avoid prefix collisions.

findings.title: Unclosed quote in match string is a prefix match, may be unintended
findings.description: The sigil `~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` deliberately omits the closing quote, making it a prefix match that covers both "lightning" and "lightning-fill". While likely intentional (the test renders both variants), it will also match unrelated names like "lightning-slash" logged by concurrent tests, partially undermining the stated goal of the comment. Explicitly listing both expected names would be clearer and stricter.
findings.suggestedFix:
refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")
refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning-fill")

findings.title: Icon-name scoping pattern is incomplete and can match the wrong log line
findings.description: The new assertion `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning)` narrows the match to the icon-name fragment, which is the intent. However, the pattern is missing the closing quote/bounds of the actual log message — a real log line such as `unknown icon name "lightning_other"` or `unknown icon name "lightningrod"` would still match this substring. More importantly, because the pattern omits any anchoring to the full token, an unrelated concurrent test logging an empty/partial unknown-icon message that happens to begin with 'lightning' would still trip or, conversely, a legitimately different random suffix could silently pass. For exact scoping, match the full token including the trailing quote, e.g. `assert log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")` (plus `refute` on the absence case). Also note `with_log/1` captures process-global Logger output across concurrently running tests, so consider this line's assertion remains inherently racy if two tests can log unknown icons concurrently — the narrowest robust fix is to match the complete token.

findings.title: Log assertion still matches icon names with the same prefix
findings.description: The scoped substring omits the closing quote after `lightning`, so it also matches unrelated messages such as `unknown icon name "lightning-fill"` or `unknown icon name "lightning-bolt"`. A concurrent test logging either name can therefore still fail this test, contrary to the stated goal of matching only the icon rendered by this row.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the closing quote in the expected log text, for example: `refute log =~ ~s(unknown icon name "lightning")`.
